messages:
anya: heads up — HF->Redwood conversion for mosaic-7b-chat caused a PPL/regression on tests with combining marks (e.g. languages with accents). quick repro below.

anya: ```py
# raw string with combining acute (e + \u0301)
s = 'e\u0301 test'
print(s)  # e01 test (visual)
# hf tokenizer (before conversion)
print(hf_tok.encode(s))  # example: [345, 12, ...]
# redwood tokenizer (after conversion)
print(rw_tok.encode(s))  # example: [98, 255, 13, ...]
```

mike: can you paste actual token ids (even a short slice)? curious if it's splitting the combining mark into separate bytes.

anya: pasted small excerpt:
```
hf: [210, 45]            # single token for 'e\u0301' + next
redwood: [92, 128, 45]   # seems like byte-fallback inserted separate bytes before spacing
```

katie: interesting — two likely culprits: unicode normalization order (NFC vs NFD/NFKC) and byte-fallback pretokenizer running before normalization in our conversion tool. HF tokenizers usually normalize to NFC first, then apply pre-tokenization.

ben: yep. if byte-fallback runs first it will map the combining mark to raw bytes and break the grapheme cluster. that will cascade into eval regressions and weird quantization alignment.

anya: i checked the converted config.json — the original HF tokenizer had: \"normalizer\": {\"type\": \"nfc\"} and \"pre_tokenizer\": [{\"type\":\"whitespace\"}, {\"type\":\"byte_fallback\"}]. our converter dropped the normalizer field and reordered to run `byte_fallback` earlier.

mike: ouch. so conversion script is not preserving the normalizer and ordering. small change should fix.

convert-bot: conversion log: \"mapping pre_tokenizer: byte_fallback -> redwood_byte_fallback (default run_at='pre')\"  (automated mapping, no normalizer emitted)

katie: suggested quick fixes:
- preserve `normalizer` entry (force NFC)
- ensure normalization runs before any byte-level fallbacks
- add unit tests with combining mark examples and CJK/emoji edge cases

anya: i can open a patch. plan: update conversion script to keep normalizer block, insert an explicit `unicode_normalize: nfc` step before byte fallback, and add a tiny test harness that compares hf_tokenizer.encode vs converted_tokenizer.encode on a few strings.

ben: also add a note in docs about special_tokens mapping for chat templates — we lost a `\u0120` (special leading-space token) mapping in one converted model which changes chat templates. that bit affected generation spacing.

mike: can we run a quick quant/throughput regression after fixing? want to be sure we didn't accidentally change the runtime path or kernel selection because token ids shifted.

anya: yes — i'll open PR and trigger the onboarding-eval workflow. assigning to ben for runtime/quant smoke, katie for eval delta checks. i'll add the failing example to the PR description.

katie: thanks — adding a short eval checklist to PR:
- token id parity on tricky strings
- zero-shot ppl on multilingual dev set
- chat-template spacing tests
- embedding similarity sanity for accents

ben: :thumbsup: will kick off a quick 4x batch quant run once PR lands.

anya: thanks all — sorry for the noise, this one was subtle. will link PR here when ready. :sparkles:
